title: Wu
capsule: The state of Wu was a polity in the lower Yangtze delta during the Spring and Autumn period, traditionally founded by descendants of the Zhou royal house at modern Suzhou. Under King Helü (r. 514–496 BCE) and his general Sun Tzu, Wu developed a powerful military that sacked the Chu capital Ying in 506 BCE, briefly making Wu the dominant power in eastern China. Helü's son Fuchai (r. 495–473 BCE) extended Wu's reach northward but was eventually defeated and killed by the resurgent state of Yue under Goujian in 473 BCE, extinguishing the Wu ruling line.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Wu's core territory in the lower Yangtze is well attested in the Zuozhuan and Shiji; precise boundaries are reconstructed and subject to scholarly debate, particularly regarding northern expansion under Fuchai.
